Colt Shelby

Libertarian candidate for Governor, Arkansas · Challenger

Drill site manager in the oil and gas industry; farm owner

Colt Shelby is a Libertarian from Cecil in Franklin County, Arkansas. He works in the oil and gas industry and owns a farm. He opposed the state's proposed 3,000-bed prison in Franklin County, and the Libertarian Party of Arkansas nominated him for governor at its convention on February 22, 2026, which put him on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot.

Where Shelby stands

Taxes and cost of living
Proposes ending the sales tax on used cars and raising Arkansas' standard deduction to match the federal one, aimed at helping the middle class.
Taxes and cost of living
Questions whether recent tax cuts have given households real relief from utility, insurance and housing costs. Says the state should 'work on true affordability' rather than small grocery savings.
Education / LEARNS Act and Education Freedom Accounts
Supports making Education Freedom Accounts income-based to scale the program back. Says the focus should be on public schools and argues that adding money alone does not improve them.
Education
Proposes restructuring the state education department so more decisions are made locally, and having it led by an Arkansas native who knows the state's public school system.
Prisons / Franklin County prison project
Opposes the proposed Franklin County prison project.
Prisons and public safety
Says he would consider amending the 2023 Protect Arkansas Act. Argues that literacy is linked to incarceration and supports investing in child care so children start building reading skills early.
Maternal and child health
Supports extending postpartum Medicaid coverage to 12 months, saying other states already provide it.
Health care / Medicaid
Supports converting the ARHOME program to fee-for-service and creating a Medicaid team. Proposes one-on-one career counselors to help 18- to 35-year-olds find jobs that include insurance.
State spending
Says state government has grown by 7% under Gov. Sanders while corrections and the Department of Human Services remain short-staffed.
Economy and communities / Agriculture
Calls for a new state Secretary of Agriculture who, he says, would be more attentive to farmers in need.

Background

  • Libertarian nominee for Governor of Arkansas, nominated at the party's convention on February 22, 2026
  • Worked on drilling rigs for Thornton Drilling (Van Buren) for about 16 years, then for a Houston-based oil company; now a drill site manager
  • Owns a farm
  • Grew up in Cecil, Arkansas; graduated from high school
  • Filed a lawsuit over the timing of the special election for the late Sen. Gary Stubblefield's state Senate seat
